articleSection: How Google Decides Who Shows Up
Turn Your Website Into a Portfolio That Takes Inquiries
Reviews From Past Clients Become Your Next Booking
@graph.articleBody: Referrals built your business: a bride tells her sister, a venue manager passes your name along. That is a great way to book events, but you do not control it. When it slows down, you have nothing to turn up. This guide adds a second way in: being found by a stranger who types "event planner near me" plus your town into Google. Key Takeaways - Local search is mainly decided by relevance, distance and prominence. Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. - If you meet clients at their venues or at a coffee shop, you are a service-area business. Google tells you to remove your address from the profile in that case. - Your website is where a planner proves taste. Give your work, your services and your areas their own pages, and make the inquiry step easy. -

mainEntity.name: How do event planners get clients online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mainly by being found when someone searches for a planner in their area. That means a verified Google Business Profile with the right address setup, a website with portfolio pages and a way to inquire, and reviews from past clients. Referrals still matter, and this adds a way for strangers to find you.

mainEntity.name: Should an event planner show a home address on Google?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you do not serve customers at your home address, Google says to remove your address from your Business Profile. A service-area business should hide its business address from customers, so most planners who work from home keep their address private.

mainEntity.name: Can I offer a discount for a review?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says offering free or discounted goods or services in exchange for reviews is strictly prohibited. Ask every client in the same way, with your profile's review link or QR code, and do not offer anything in return.

mainEntity.name: How many service areas can I list?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says you can set up to 20 service areas based on cities, postal codes or other areas you serve. List only the places where you really plan events.
